newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says no deal done on CIA shooter snatch.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says no deal done on CIA shooter snatch.

text.p: Interior Minister Shujaat Hussain denied on Thursday that Pakistan had done a deal with the United States to allow last month's arrest of a Pakistani national charged with killing two CIA workers and wounding three others in a shooting spree outside the spy agency's headquarters.

But, speaking in parliament, he declined to disclose the details of the arrest of Mir Aimal Kansi, maintaining a government silence over the affair 18 days after the man was reported to have been picked up from a hotel by agents of U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) with the help of Pakistani commandos.

Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government has come under fire from opposition politicians and newspapers for allegedly handing over Kansi without fulfilling legal formalities under Pakistan's extradition law and compromising national sovereignty.
Some commentators had suggested that Islamabad made a deal with U.S. authorities in return for a concession in some other matter.
But Hussain said in the Senate (upper house): "No deal was involved in this. As far as Pakistan's sovereignty is concerned, we will not compromise."

He refused to give details because the matter had become sub judice after several petitions challenging the arrest were filed before high courts in Kansi's home province of Baluchistan and Punjab province.
"Our sovereignty has been shattered," an opposition Senator from Baluchistan, Abdul Haye Baluch, said in his speech.
"People all over the country feel themselves unsafe," he said. "Tomorrow any political worker disliked by America can be taken away."

A judge on in Fairfax, Virginia on Wednesday set a November 3 trial date for Kansi, 33, who was apprehended in Pakistan and brought back to the United States last month to face murder and other criminal charges that carry the death penalty.

He has been charged in the January 25, 1993, morning rush hour shooting outside Central Intelligence Agency headquarters at Langley, Virginia, just outside Washington. All but one of the victims were CIA employees.
